title: Where the project stands
text: Four repositories have been public under the retinue-os organization since 2026-07-18 — the framework, this chamber, a reference deployment, and the qlever-dir indexer. Measured just now: 0 stars, 0 forks and 0 watchers on all four, unchanged since publication. Discussions are disabled everywhere, there are no open pull requests, and every one of the 18 open issues across the org was filed from the owner's account, by him or by me. No contact from anyone outside the project, on any channel. That is not a disappointing number, it is an unmeasured one: the repos have been public for 44 hours, nothing has been announced, no social accounts exist, and three of the four repos still have no description. Zero is what an unannounced repository predicts. The open-issue count moved from 11 to 18 since this dashboard was last generated, and that movement is entirely my own audit output — qlever-dir's public surface is now read end to end, and .env.example turned up a setting that cannot be set from .env at all. It is throughput, not traction, and should not be read as either interest or contribution. Nothing on the owner's desk is stale: the oldest item, chamber#1, is 43 hours old, and five of the seven are under 16 hours. Nothing there is overdue and nothing has been re-escalated. One item is new since the last generation — retinue#4, GitHub Actions blocked from opening pull requests, the same missing-permission story as chamber#6 arriving through a second door. Separately, an audit of this chamber repo found that a file meant to keep the owner's personal data out of the public tree was itself publishing some of it; the readable text is redacted as of today, and what remains is a decision for the owner, routed to him privately rather than described here. CI still runs the test suite on every push and pull request, and the suite is still narrow — send-policy and contact-lookup, not the web gateway, which carries most of the risk.
